solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spare part nice used in one that goes flat out

indicators.note: letters that have been used are knocked about and reshaped, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic's spare part, nicely used in a car that drives flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat out' suggests top speed, but a rug lies fully flat on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug from Iran is laid out flat across a floor, a cryptic way of describing floor covering.

clue.text: Knight for one under spell in historical drama

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first, so it comes after it

parts.note: a spell is a stretch of time, a period
a knight is one example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: A knight under an enchantment, as in an old costume drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks magical but means a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or play set in a past era, with its costumes and manners, is called by this name.

clue.text: Fanatical attack involving bishop

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the attack word holds the bishop letter

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A zealot launches an attack that drags in a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extreme and frenzied in their views is described as rabid, a synonym of fanatical.

clue.text: New clue I can't gradually introduce

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters of these words take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A solver complains they can't take a new clue in slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea by patient repetition is to fix it slowly in someone's mind.

clue.text: Excellent plunder in some British region's capital

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed in the region's letters

parts.note: NI stands for Northern Ireland, a region of the United Kingdom
A1 means first-rate; crosswords read it as the letters AI
to plunder is to rob

explanation.surface: Excellent looting takes place in a British region's chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; the region's own capital is Belfast, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Kenya, making it a national capital.

clue.text: Scandinavians, heading to centre in Peak District

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word for the Scandinavians travels to the middle

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark, in Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Scandinavian visitors head into the middle of England's Peak District.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is an English national park, but here the phrase describes a mountainous region.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American range is a district full of peaks, a playful re-reading of an English place name.

clue.text: Oil suppliers spot south-east river rising

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: Someone spots that a river in the south-east is rising, maybe near oil supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pipes carrying crude from wells to refineries are what deliver oil.

clue.text: Crew unable to finish meal

indicators.note: the word for the crew cannot reach its end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a crew is a team working together

explanation.surface: A crew too exhausted to finish their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the evening meal or a light afternoon snack is often called by this drink's name.

clue.text: Grump driver ultimately bundled into carriage

indicators.note: being bundled into something means being pushed inside it

parts.note: a cab was originally a horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word driver

explanation.surface: A grumpy driver is finally shoved into a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab, as in a crabby person, is an irritable sourpuss.

clue.text: One young fan out for a walk in park

parts.note: a child is one who is young
to splay is to spread out like a fan

explanation.surface: A young fan heads out for a stroll in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk in park' is the idiom for something easy, not a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Doorbell broken — here one's invited to knock?

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of the word are reassembled

explanation.surface: The doorbell is broken, so visitors are invited to knock instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like rapping at the door, but in British slang it also means having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a place where clients come for sex, the slang sense of knocking.

clue.text: Eastern ruler last month placed in clinic

indicators.note: the month abbreviation is put inside the clinic word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of clinic
ult, short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: An Eastern potentate was admitted to a clinic last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch of a Muslim country, such as Oman or Brunei, holds this title.

clue.text: Old people struggling along with boys receiving a kiss

indicators.note: struggling suggests flailing about, so the letters of along are jumbled
the boys' word takes the a and the kiss inside it

parts.note: sons are boys
X is the kiss symbol at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Elderly folk struggle along while boys are given a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The early English peoples of the post-Roman era are a historical, long-gone population.

clue.text: Connoisseur wants item offered at low price first

parts.note: a special is a discounted item on offer
1st is the short form of first, read as IST

explanation.surface: An expert wants the bargain item before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert with deep knowledge of one field is an authority, as a connoisseur is.

clue.text: Sausage sandwiches with it in drink — thanks!

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between two layers, so the drink encloses another piece
the fashionable word goes in the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink
hip means fashionable, with it
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone is served sausage sandwiches with a drink and says thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food next to 'Sausage' but signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin pork banger, often served at British Christmas dinner, is called by this name.

clue.text: Attempt to imprison every royal woman — there's a word for it?

definitions.text: Attempt to imprison every royal woman — there's a word for it?

indicators.note: the attempt word locks the other two pieces inside it

parts.note: to try is to attempt
each means every
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Plotting to lock up the Queen: surely there's a word for such a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's sovereign, such as by seizing her, is disloyal betrayal of trust, a synonym for this word.

clue.text: Drink nothing in such dangerous areas?

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog drink
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is drinking nothing advised in dangerous places?
explanation.definitionFit: Places too risky to enter are called by this term, so it describes such areas.

clue.text: Lovely being by island

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A beautiful creature living by an island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth this is a beautiful fairy or spirit, a lovely being.

clue.text: Look for something to say

definitions.meaning: a look on one's face, as in a pained look
a phrase or idiom one might utter

explanation.surface: Looking around for something to say.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a facial look and a turn of phrase, two separate senses.

clue.text: Long to receive explanation for viewer's complaint

indicators.note: the longing word takes the explanation into itself

parts.note: to long for is to pine
a key explains, as a map's key does

explanation.surface: Longing for an explanation of what's wrong with one's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' suggests a TV watcher but means anyone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjunctivitis, an eye infection, is an ailment of the one who sees.

clue.text: Compensate rabble "discontented" with putsch

indicators.note: with its contents taken out only the outer letters of rabble remain

parts.note: a putsch is a coup, a seizure of power

explanation.surface: A discontented mob is paid off after a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up for a loss is to regain or reimburse it.

clue.text: Two characters abroad initially pursuing model

parts.note: pi and nu are two letters of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of pursuing is taken

explanation.surface: Two people overseas first start chasing a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamour model whose poster is stuck on a wall is called this.

clue.text: Man going commando? Might one hear that?

indicators.note: the question asks what one hears, so the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: going commando is slang for wearing no underwear, being without knickers

explanation.surface: A man goes without underwear: might one overhear that?
explanation.walkthrough: Knickers are British for women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Love shown by wise man in Siouan language

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man shows love for a Native American tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Osage people of the Great Plains belongs to the Siouan family.

clue.text: Distant relative, super-polite, smuggles in ecstasy

parts.note: great is an informal synonym for super

indicators.note: the polite word secretly holds the drug letter inside

parts.note: nice can mean polite and pleasant
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A far-off relation, terribly polite, is caught smuggling drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister's granddaughter is a relation two generations removed, a distant kin.

clue.text: Men climbing caught by enormous bird

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters read upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Climbers are snatched up by a giant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabian legend this huge bird could carry off elephants, as in Sinbad's tales.

clue.text: Not much material in first thirteen letters?

definitions.meaning: the tiniest particle of matter, so a very small amount
the alphabet from A through to M, read as a phrase

explanation.surface: Is there little substance in the first part of the alphabet?
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of matter is a tiny particle, so very little stuff; and A to M spans thirteen letters.

clue.text: Cheesy samples cooked the French way

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients have been mixed and transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheesy tasters prepared in Gallic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French way' looks like a cooking style but is a Paris avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous avenue in Paris is literally a road in France, the Elysian Fields.
